title: Recognition of Value Returned by a Package Operator — Travel Protection Plans
content:
When the declared trip cost of a Travel Protection Plans certificate is corrected, the amounts the operator has returned otherwise than on the surrender of the journey are recognised at a share, and that share is read from the vacation package the cover was bought alongside, one of the Vacation Package Products.

Those amounts are the sums the operator has returned to the traveller together with the credits it has given back, less what it returned on the surrender of the journey itself.

Where the package returns value to the original form of payment and an amount has been returned against it, the amounts the operator has returned otherwise than on the surrender of the journey are recognised in full, at 100 per cent.

Where the package returns value only as a future travel credit and the credit standing open against it may still be redeemed after the last day of the journey insured, those amounts are recognised at three quarters, 75 per cent.

Where neither holds, those amounts are recognised at nothing, 0 per cent.

## The graded recognition

| The form in which the package returns value | The further test | Recognised at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The original form of payment | An amount has been returned against the package | 100 per cent |
| A future travel credit only | The credit standing open may still be redeemed after the last day of the journey insured | 75 per cent |
| Neither of those | — | 0 per cent |

## Cases

A case at full recognition: the package returns value to the original form of payment, and money has in fact been returned against it. The whole of what the operator returned otherwise than on the surrender of the journey is recognised.

A case at three quarters: the package returns value only as a future travel credit, and the credit still open against it expires after the last day of the journey insured, so it is a credit the traveller can still use. Three quarters of those amounts are recognised.

A case at nothing: the package returns value only as a future travel credit whose open credit expires on or before the last day of the journey insured. Neither of the first two cases is reached, and nothing at all of those amounts is recognised. The same follows where the package returns value to the original form of payment but nothing has been returned against it.

Hypothetically, where the operator returned 500.00 USD to the traveller and gave back a credit of 300.00 USD, and 200.00 USD of that was returned on the surrender of the journey, the amounts returned otherwise than on the surrender come to 600.00 USD. Recognised in full they are 600.00 USD; at three quarters, 450.00 USD; at nothing, 0.00 USD.
